## Rules that apply to every prompt

# Project: 26.humza.website (birthday quiz)

## Stack

- npm workspaces + Turborepo (npm only, never pnpm/yarn)
- apps/web: React 19 + Vite. Routes: /play (phones), /screen (projector), /host (control panel)
- apps/worker: Hono on Cloudflare Workers + one Durable Object class `Room` (WebSocket Hibernation API, SQLite storage, alarms)
- packages/shared: Zod schemas, pure game logic (reducer, scoring, awards, time sync, rate limiter, troll rules)
- packages/emails: React Email templates, sent via Resend
- Post-game persistence: Neon Postgres + Drizzle, RLS enabled on every table
- Photos: Cloudflare R2
- Tests: Vitest (unit + component via Testing Library + jsdom), @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers (DO/Worker), Playwright (e2e), Node bot harness (load)

## Architecture rules

- The server is authoritative. Clients send intents and render state. They never compute scores, timers or phase changes.
- All game logic is a pure reducer in packages/shared: `reduce(state, event, now) -> { state, effects }`. The DO is a thin shell that feeds events in and executes effects (broadcast, set alarm, persist). This is what makes everything unit-testable.
- Time is always injected (`now: number`), never `Date.now()` inside logic.
- Browser APIs (wakeLock, vibrate, getUserMedia, Audio) are wrapped in small adapters so tests can mock them.

## Testing rules (non-negotiable)

- Every feature has at least one test file, named in the phase prompt. Write the tests first or alongside the code, never after "it works".
- Never skip, `.only`, or delete a failing test to get green. Fix the code or ask.
- Pure logic → plain Vitest. DO behaviour → vitest-pool-workers. UI → Testing Library. Cross-device flows → Playwright.
- A phase is done only when `npm run test:unit` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Scripts

- Naming: `<domain>:<action>` (e.g. `test:unit`, `questions:check`, `email:preview`, `dev:jump`)
- A fresh checkout is prepared with `npm install`, then `npm run setup`. Setup installs dependencies, syncs environment files, generates a missing local client API key, copies agent instructions, generates Worker types, installs Playwright Chromium, and migrates and seeds the local database. It leaves an existing local key unchanged and does not deploy or upload secrets.

- This is a separate birthday project. Never change LifeSmart, use its production resources or copy its pupil-specific rules into this project.
- The plan's agreed decisions take precedence over its suggested defaults. Later explicit user decisions take precedence over both. Record material implementation choices.
- Baseer presents and Humza controls. Guests play individually. No pods, guest accounts, CMS, compulsory scoring floor or automatic score multipliers.
- Keep questions in versioned server-side TypeScript. Public question data is a deliberate projection that excludes correct answers, scoring secrets and future reveals.
- One Worker serves the application and API; one SQLite-backed Durable Object owns each room. Neon and email stay outside the live guest-action path. Image/audio processing also stays outside it.
- Persist accepted actions before success acknowledgements. Make retries idempotent. Memory is a cache. Use one durable scheduler to own all room alarms.
- Identity uses random game-scoped credentials. Device information is separately associated context, never an identity fingerprint or authority for scoring.
- Use React, TypeScript, Vite, Hono, Cloudflare Workers/Durable Objects/R2, Neon, Better Auth and Resend as specified in the plan. Use a small shared validation package and consistent styling primitives. Verify current official documentation when implementing version-sensitive APIs; pin compatible dependencies and retain the lockfile.
- Use domain folders, British English, accessible controls and clear phone states. Include reduced-motion support and optional audio. Keep secrets and personal diagnostics off the projector.
- Do not open, quote, or commit secret files such as `.env`, `.dev.vars`, private keys, or credential files. Example templates may be read.
- `artifacts/` is local check output and is gitignored: Playwright reports, probe logs, screenshots, and Miniflare storage. A path that is already tracked stays in the index until it is removed. After changing `.gitignore`, or when `git status` still lists a tracked ignored path such as a Playwright `.last-run.json`, run `npm run git:drop-ignored`. That command removes those paths from the index and leaves the files on disk. Do not commit that output.
- `npm run git:sync` fetches from every remote, prunes deleted remote-tracking branches, and deletes local branches whose upstream is gone. It keeps the checked-out branch, `master`, `main`, and branches that were never pushed. A branch Git still considers unmerged is kept until `npm run git:sync -- --force`.
- Work in the existing implementation. Do not create competing state stores, socket clients, auth factories, schedulers, schemas or score engines for each new feature.
- Keep production paths real. Deterministic local fakes are allowed only behind explicit test/development adapters; they must not silently succeed in deployed environments.
- Implement, run relevant checks, fix failures and update documentation. Do not rewrite unrelated work or weaken checks to obtain a pass.
- No deployments, paid resource creation or changes to unrelated remote resources are implied by Prompts 01-18. Missing external credentials should not prevent completing locally testable work; report precisely what remains unverified.
- Agent instructions are edited in `.agents`. Run `npm run agents:sync` afterwards. Do not hand-edit the generated copies.
- Layout: `.agents/rules/05-structure.md`. Performance and workflow: `.agents/rules/55-agent-workflow.md` plus `60-perf-*.md`. Goal: zero perceptible slowdown for about 80 phones. Do not restructure the tree in a rules-only change.
- At the end of every stage update `docs/build-progress.md`: status, files/interfaces added, decisions/defaults, commands and results, manual verification, unresolved issues and the exact next stage. Never label an unrun check as passed.
- Final response for each stage: what now works, how to run/try it, what was verified and any concrete remaining limitation. Do not automatically begin the next prompt.

# Codebase structure

This tree is **feature-first**. A new round, screen, or message type has one obvious home. Do not add a parallel store, socket client, scheduler, or score engine. Prefer `git mv` for moves. After a layout change, update this file, the perf-rule globs (`60-perf-*.md`), `apps/web/src/admin/features.ts`, and run `npm run agents:sync`.

`scripts/check-structure.mjs` (`npm run check:structure`, also part of `npm run lint`) enforces the top-level allowlists and the import boundaries below.

## Import boundaries (also ESLint)

- `apps/web` must not import `apps/api` or server auth (`create-auth`, `better-auth/db`).

## How to add a new round

1. **Mechanic** — Reuse `choice` / `typed` / `slider` / `rank` / `vote` / `guess` / `duel` / `finale` / `wordle` / `kart` / `chess` if it fits. Read `docs/question-authoring.md`.
2. **Pack file** — `apps/api/src/questions/packs/birthday/<id>.ts` with the helper in `authoring.ts`. Register on `catalogue` only (not `order` while drafting).
3. **Server runtime** — If it needs new scoring or persistence, add or extend `apps/api/src/questions/<mechanic>/` (or the existing quiz module). Wire `PartyRoom` through the existing plugin/command path. Persist before ack.
4. **Shared contract** — Zod + pure reducer in `packages/shared/src/<mechanic>/` if phones and the Worker share shapes. Export from `index.ts`. Keep secrets off the public snapshot.
5. **Phone + stage** — Ordinary UI in `apps/web/src/play/` (widgets in `play/controls/`). Custom look: `play/designs/<slug>.tsx` + `customPresentationIds`. Heavy engine: `apps/web/src/<mechanic>/` and `React.lazy` from `guest-play.tsx` / `stage-play.tsx`.
6. **Host** — Admin see/manage/rehearse in the same change (`adminFeatures` `owns` the folders). Host-only fields only for `audience === "control"`.
7. **Check** — `npm run content:check`, unit tests, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (includes structure), `npm run budget:web` if the client graph changed.

Do not start a second WebSocket, a client-side score, or a new question CMS.

# Admin coverage

Every feature ships with its admin view in the same change. A feature is not done until the host can **see** it, **manage** it and **rehearse** it from `/admin`, without asking guests to help.

## The registry is the source of truth

`apps/web/src/admin/features.ts` lists every feature (`adminFeatures`). The sidebar, the page titles and the room overview cards are built from it. Each entry has:

- `id`, `label`, `scope` (`global` under `/admin`, `room` under `/admin/rooms/:gameId`) and `path`.
- `summary`: what the page shows, in one sentence.
- `rehearsal`: what the host can try with no guests (a preview, sample, demo or dry run). Be concrete. "None" is not acceptable. If something truly needs live guests, say how to do it with a second browser tab.
- `owns`: the top-level source folders the feature lives in (`apps/api/src/<domain>`, `apps/web/src/<domain>`). Each folder belongs to exactly one feature.
- `status` (room features): a short live line for the overview card, read from the host snapshot.

Shared plumbing that is not a feature goes in `adminExempt` with a reason. Do not exempt something to avoid building its view.

`apps/web/src/admin/features.test.ts` enforces this. It fails when a source folder has no owner, a folder is owned twice, an owned folder no longer exists, a feature has no summary or rehearsal, or an `/admin` route and a registry entry do not match. Never weaken the test to get a pass; add the view.

## What a feature's admin view must have

1. **See.** The current state, live from the host snapshot (`useAdminRoom`) for room features, or from a validated section read (`readSection`) for global ones. Show counts, who did what and when, and anything waiting on the host. Include history, not just what is happening now.
2. **Manage.** Every host action for the feature, as a host command (`execute(...)` → `/api/rooms/play` → `readHostDetails` → `applyHostAction`). Commands are receipted, validated again inside the room, and roll back on error. Give each one a notice in `command-notices.ts` and a `CommandScope` for its feedback.
3. **Rehearse.** A way to try it without guests: render the real phone and stage component with sample data (frame previews, troll previews, question rehearsal), or a demo or dry-run command. Use real components, never a mock-up that can drift.
4. **Safe defaults.** Anything that reaches the projector or guests can be switched off or undone from the page.

## Server side

- Host-only data goes in the snapshot only for `audience === "control"`, as an optional field on `lobbySnapshotSchema` with exact Zod limits. Never send it to the stage or guests.
- Add host actions to the `commands` list in `routes.ts`, to `readHostDetails` (validate every field), to `PartyRoom.hostAction` and to `applyHostAction`. Validate again in the domain function; the room does not trust its caller.

## Tests for each feature's admin view

- A room spec for each host command: success, refusal and replay.
- A component test for the admin page using `controls.test-support.tsx` (`setupControls`, `mountControls`): each control sends the right command.
- A snapshot test proving host-only fields are absent for stage and guest audiences.

## Checklist for a new feature

1. Build the feature.
2. Add or extend its entry in `adminFeatures`, with `owns` covering its folders. A new top-level `apps/web/src/<domain>` or `apps/api/src/<domain>` folder also needs the allowlist in `.agents/rules/05-structure.md` and `scripts/check-structure.mjs`.
3. Add the route in `apps/web/src/routes.tsx`, and the path to `admin-return.ts`.
4. Build the see, manage and rehearse view.
5. Add the tests above, and run `features.test.ts`.
6. Update `docs/data-inventory.md` if it stores anything new, and `docs/build-progress.md`.

# Agent workflow and performance contract

This party must feel instant on mid-range phones and the projector with about **80 concurrent guests**. Zero perceptible slowdown is the goal: a tap, a phase change, a reconnect, and a kart frame must not hitch, freeze, or wait on work that belongs off the main thread or off the live room path.

Do not reorganise folders in a performance-rules change. The layout is `.agents/rules/05-structure.md`. Prefer a module's job (`openRoomSocket`, `PartyRoom`, `KartCanvas`) over a brittle deep path when both would do. After a structural move, update this file's globs and `05-structure.md` in the same PR.

Detailed, file-scoped rules live in `.agents/rules/60-perf-*.md` (synced to `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`). Edit `.agents`, then run `npm run agents:sync`. Do not hand-edit generated copies. `CLAUDE.md` only points at `AGENTS.md`.

## Workflow guardrails

- **Small, focused PRs.** One concern per branch. Do not mix a mechanic change with a folder move, a dependency bump, and a visual rewrite.
- **Never push to `master` or `main`.** Open a PR against `master`. Do not merge unless the owner asked.
- **No force-push** to shared branches. No `--force` / `--force-with-lease` on `master`.
- **Do not deploy**, create paid cloud resources, or change staging/production secrets unless the owner asked in this turn.
- **Do not add Playwright or other E2E/browser runners.** The owner has prohibited them. Prove behaviour with typecheck, lint, Vitest (jsdom / workers pool), and existing Node script tests.
- **Before finishing:** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and the unit tests that cover what you touched (`npm run test:unit` and/or `npm run test -w @26/api`). Run `npm run build` when the client graph, public assets, or Vite config changed so `budget:web` runs.
- **Do not delete, rewrite, or “clean up” unrelated code** to make a diff look tidy. Do not skip, `.only`, or delete a failing test to get green.
- **Ask (or stop and report) before a large refactor**, a new state store, a second socket client, a new scheduler, or a competing score engine. Work in the existing modules.
- **Do not copy LifeSmart**, pupil-specific rules, or unrelated repos into this tree.
- British English in guest/stage copy. Keep secrets, answer keys, and personal diagnostics off the projector.

## Performance contract (every feature)

1. **Server is authoritative.** Phones send intents. They do not compute scores, timers, or phase changes. Optimistic UI may show _sending_, never _accepted_, until the ack.
2. **Hot paths stay hot.** Guest answers, kart inputs, and broadcasts stay inside the Durable Object. Neon, email, R2 processing, and archives stay off that path.
3. **Eighty phones are the load model.** A message, query, or render that is cheap for one guest is expensive when it runs eighty times. Batch, patch, and reuse.
4. **Main thread stays interactive.** Stockfish, image decode, GLB parse, and heavy JSON do not run on the UI thread during a question. Game loops use `requestAnimationFrame` and refs, not React state every frame.
5. **Join stays thin.** `/play` and `/screen` must not download kart, chess, or admin. Lazy-load per round. Warm during the intro beat, not on first tap of “send”.
6. **Perceived speed.** Instant press feedback, stable layout (no CLS), reconnect with jitter, skeletons that match the final chrome. The dock send button never waits on a bundle.

## Scoped rules

### Server-side question packs

Applies to `apps/api/src/questions/**/*.ts`.

# Questions

- Keep the party script in versioned TypeScript in this folder. There is no CMS and no client-side question pack.
- Public snapshots exclude correct answers, scoring secrets, and future reveals.
- Do not copy answer keys or truth nicknames into `apps/web`.
- The pack a room plays is the one named by its stored version. The illustrative demo stays `demo-2026-09-22` until a birthday version is explicitly released.
- New party questions are files in `apps/api/src/questions/packs/birthday/`, registered on the catalogue and left out of the running order while they are drafts. Do not invent party questions, and do not edit the demo pack to hold them.

### Question authoring workflow

Applies to `apps/api/src/questions/**/*.ts` and `docs/question-authoring.md`.

# Question authoring

Read `docs/question-authoring.md` before adding or editing a question. Party questions are TypeScript files, not a CMS.

Recognise:

- "Next question idea: …"
- "Add a question where …"
- "Make this question ready."
- "Move this question before …"
- "Change the answer/options for …"
- "Now customise the design of this question."

For a new idea:

1. Read the birthday manifest, `authoring.ts`, `defaults.ts`, and any related question.
2. Choose an existing mechanic when it fits: choice (with a correct, poll, threshold or push-your-luck outcome), typed, wordle, slider, rank, vote, guess, duel, or finale.
3. Create `apps/api/src/questions/packs/birthday/<id>.ts` with the matching helper. The id and filename are a stable slug, with no running-order number.
4. Apply defaults from `defaults.ts` for ordinary settings the user did not specify.
5. Keep the user's wording. Record a material assumption in the question file only when it changes the mechanic.
6. Record a missing answer or asset with `{ missing: { code, name, detail } }` or a required media ref that has no `asset`. Do not invent the fact, the person, or the file.
7. Import the question in `packs/birthday/manifest.ts` `catalogue`. Do not add a draft to `order`. Do not change `startDemo`, the demo pack, a room, or a deployment.
8. Run `npm run content:check`.
9. Report the id, mechanic, draft or ready status, and anything still missing.

Wordle uses `wordleQuestion` with a supplied five-letter uppercase target. The default is six guesses, two minutes and 100 points for a solve. Keep the target and dictionary server-side; never substitute ordinary typed matching. Use the real authenticated phone rehearsal to check feedback.

Ask a short question only when the ambiguity changes the meaning or the mechanic. Otherwise save a draft.

If the interaction is not one of these mechanics, explain the gap and still save a draft. Do not force the wrong mechanic or rewrite scoring.

A later edit finds the existing file by id. Reordering changes `order` in the manifest only. "Make this question ready" fills real supplied facts and, once it validates, still does not enter `order` unless the user asked to include it.

"Now customise the design of this question" keeps the same id and mechanic. Add the slug to `customPresentationIds` in `packages/shared`, set `presentation` on the question, write the design in `apps/web/src/play/designs/<slug>.tsx` with the shared kit, and register it in `designs/registry.ts`. Follow the full-screen question experience rule. Check the actual question in Admin → Question packs → Phone preview, plus `/design` for stand-in reveal states in development. Do not put the answer key in the client.

Do not edit a released pack's question files in place. A content change needs a new version id. Rooms keep the version they stored.

### Worker, room, and shared validation

Applies to `apps/api/**/*.ts` and `packages/shared/**/*.ts`.

# Worker and room

- One Worker serves the application and API. One SQLite-backed Durable Object owns each room. One durable scheduler owns all room alarms.
- Live-path cost: follow `.agents/rules/61-perf-realtime.md` and `62-perf-server.md`. About 80 phones share one object; batch writes, patch snapshots, keep kart ticks off full fan-out.
- Persist an accepted action before its success acknowledgement. Retries use the same idempotency key.
- Neon, email, and image or audio processing stay outside the live guest-action path.
- Read configuration from Worker bindings. Do not read `process.env` in `apps/api/src` or `packages/shared/src`.
- Staging and production `vars` hold `APP_ENV` and `MEDIA_BUCKET_NAME` only. Required secret names are not stored as empty vars.
- A local fake must refuse to succeed when `APP_ENV` is `staging` or `production`.

### Phone, stage, and admin screens

Applies to `apps/web/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/**/*.tsx`.

# Web app

- Use British English, accessible controls, and clear phone states. Support reduced motion. Keep audio optional.
- Keep phones and the projector instant: `.agents/rules/60-perf-web.md`, `63-perf-game-loops.md`, `64-perf-assets.md`. Lazy-load kart/chess, no per-frame React state, terminate workers.
- Follow the design and motion rules. Open the live library docs listed there before copying a component; ease every visible change.
- Keep secrets and personal diagnostics off the projector and the stage screen.
- Do not import server auth modules into the web app.
- Do not put answer keys, truth nicknames, or scoring secrets in client code.
- A new theme is a palette plus a skin. Follow the theme rule. Do not ship colours alone. Icons for a category or a brand come from the packs named there.

### Full-screen party questions, clear phone actions and presentation flow

Applies to `apps/web/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/**/*.css` and `apps/api/src/questions/**/*.ts` and `docs/question-authoring.md`.

# Question experience

- This is a hosted Kahoot/Jackbox-style party game: Baseer presents, Humza advances the show, guests act on their phones. Design each round as a short presentation with get-ready, answer, sending, locked-in, reveal and score beats. The server owns when each beat occurs.
- Phone questions occupy the usable screen, with one unmistakable instruction, the question and generous answer controls. Keep the primary send action in the existing phone dock. Use the shared `QuestionExperience` frame and real `GuestPlay` renderer; bespoke designs keep their own identity inside that frame.
- Make the next action explicit: “Pick one, then send”, “Slide to your estimate”, or “Locked in — watch the stage”. Clearly distinguish selected, sending and server-accepted answers. Do not label an optimistic selection accepted in a live game.
- Use deliberate space and large type. Ordinary two-to-six-option questions should fit a phone screen; long ballots, long wording, keyboard entry and enlarged text may scroll vertically. Never clip an answer or shrink essential text just to fit. Check 320, 390 and 430px widths, a short landscape viewport, safe areas and zoom.
- Keep photo, sound, recovery and troll-selection tools secondary. Incoming troll notices and escape controls remain visible. Do not make these tools compete with the question or send button.
- Each question can have its own composition, motif and interaction treatment. Do not force every design into the same card grid. Reuse shared controls, theme variables, presentation registry and mechanics; never fork the socket, score engine or scheduler for a visual.
- Animate every meaningful change: question/phase entry, option selection, input feedback, submission, waiting, reveal, score and list/layout changes. Use Motion and the existing motion kit with eased timing, springs and short staggered entrances. Keep options stable and usable while the clock runs; decorative animation must not delay an action, cover text or leave an outgoing phase interactive.
- Respect reduced motion with short opacity/colour fades, no loops, parallax or travel. Never gate meaning on animation, sound or colour alone. Keep audio optional and stage wording readable across a room.
- Admin Question packs and individual question pages must offer a phone rehearsal using the actual guest renderer and server-projected public question fields. A rehearsal is isolated: no live room, socket, score, persistence or fabricated answer key. Label stand-in players, incomplete drafts and unsupported mechanics. Do not invent slider bounds or pretend a placeholder is the finished mechanic.
- When customising a question, verify its get-ready, answering, selected, pending, accepted, paused and reveal states in the admin preview/design bench and meaningful tests. Keep answer keys, notes and future reveals out of preview payloads. Add private admin details only to their existing authenticated inspection route.

### Party UI libraries, fluid motion, and reduced-motion fallbacks

Applies to `apps/web/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/**/*.css`.

# Design and motion

Maximise the libraries below. Reach for their current components, primitives, and effects first. Install and pin a missing package when a screen needs it. Do not invent a parallel primitive kit or one-off visual language beside `apps/web/src/ui`.

Before using or copying anything, open the live site (and the specific component or API page). Do not reconstruct APIs, class names, or install commands from memory. If the page and training data disagree, the page wins.

Compose those libraries into the existing surfaces (phone, stage, host, admin, results). Do not copy LifeSmart branding. Keep British English, large tappable phone controls, and stage type readable from across a room.

Screen colours come from `apps/web/src/theme/themes.ts`. A theme also has a skin, so the chrome fits the idea. Follow the theme rule when adding or changing one. Category and brand icons come from the packs listed in that rule: Lucide, Simple Icons, Game Icons, and Material Design Icons, rendered with `@iconify/react/dist/offline`.

## Libraries to check

Primitives and motion engine:

- [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com)
- [Motion](https://motion.dev) (`motion/react`)
- [Base UI](https://base-ui.com)

Animated registries and kits (use freely, mix as needed):

- [Animate UI](https://animate-ui.com)
- [Magic UI](https://magicui.design)
- [React Bits](https://reactbits.dev)
- [Aceternity UI](https://ui.aceternity.com)
- [Origin UI](https://originui.com)
- [Kokonut UI](https://kokonutui.com)
- [Fancy Components](https://www.fancycomponents.dev)
- [Motion Primitives](https://motion-primitives.com)
- [Cult UI](https://www.cult-ui.com)
- [Animata](https://animata.design)
- [21st.dev](https://21st.dev)

Targeted motion utilities:

- [Number Flow](https://number-flow.barvian.me)
- [AutoAnimate](https://auto-animate.formkit.com)

## Fluid motion

Every visible change is eased. Nothing snaps: hover, press, focus, disabled, open/close, mount/unmount, list insert/remove/reorder, page or phase change, loading, success, and error. Subtle motion is required; instant `display`, un-eased colour cuts, and zero-duration transitions are not.

Use Motion springs or shared duration/easing tokens. Prefer enter/exit and layout animation over CSS that only styles the resting state. Decorative loops belong on the stage or idle screens, not on controls a guest must hit quickly.

```tsx
// ❌ BAD — appears and vanishes instantly
{
  open ? <Panel /> : null;
}

// ✅ GOOD — eased presence, still uses the shared panel
<AnimatePresence>
  {open ? (
    <motion.div
      initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 8 }}
      animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
      exit={{ opacity: 0, y: 8 }}
    >
      <Panel />
    </motion.div>
  ) : null}
</AnimatePresence>;
```

## Reduced motion and stage safety

Honour `prefers-reduced-motion`. Turn off loops, parallax, blur storms, and layout thrash. Keep a short opacity or colour fade for state changes so the UI still does not pop. Motion must never hide a question, option, score, or answer on the projector, and must never put secrets or personal diagnostics on stage.

### Party themes are a palette plus a skin that fits the idea

Applies to `apps/web/src/theme/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/src/theme/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/src/theme/**/*.css`.

# Themes

A theme is not a colour swap. It is a palette plus a skin that makes the shared chrome feel like the idea. Phones and the projector choose a theme separately. The choice is not pushed by the room.

Recognise:

- "Add a theme …"
- "New palette for …"
- "Make a theme where …"

Read these before editing:

- `apps/web/src/theme/themes.ts` for colours, roles, categories, and `DEFAULT_THEME_ID`
- `apps/web/src/theme/skins.ts` for families
- `apps/web/src/theme/theme-skin.css` for grounds and corner tokens
- `apps/web/src/theme/wordmark.tsx` for marks
- `apps/web/src/theme/install.ts` for how `data-theme` and `data-skin` are applied

## Palette

Add the palette in `themes.ts`. That file is the only place colour values are written.

- The id is lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. The object key matches the id. The display name may keep punctuation.
- Fill every palette role: background, foreground, muted, accent, accentForeground, highlight, highlightForeground, surface, surfaceForeground, line, mark, markQuiet.
- Set `colorScheme` from the ground. Use `light` when the ground is cream, paper, white, or yellow. Otherwise use `dark`.
- Accent and highlight are both text on the page background and fills for buttons. Both pairs need contrast, and so do their foreground colours on those fills. `mark` on `markQuiet` stays strong enough for a join code.
- List the theme in exactly one `themeCategories` group. A missing or repeated id fails the typecheck.
- Leave `DEFAULT_THEME_ID` as `26-basic` unless the user asks to change the party default.
- Do not recolour `apps/web/public/favicon.svg`. It stays the 26 basic mark.

## Skin

`26-basic` is the only plain theme. Every other theme has an entry in `skins.ts`. The map is every theme id except `26-basic`, so a new theme that only has colours fails typecheck.

Choose the skin for the idea, not for whichever family was used last.

1. Join an existing family when that ground, shape, mark, and finish already say the idea. School lines, a nightclub stripe, a terminal grid, a floodlight, and a foil edge are families. Reuse them.
2. Add a ground, shape, or mark only when no family fits. Put the ground in `theme-skin.css`, built from the theme's own variables (`--background`, `--surface`, `--accent`, `--highlight`, `--line`). Take the mark from the icon packs below. Draw a new stroke in `wordmark.tsx` only when none of those packs has a fitting icon.
3. Do not leave the new theme on the plain chrome.

The skin changes the shared frame only:

- **Ground.** A fixed layer behind the page. It never sits on a question, option, score, or answer.
- **Shape.** `--radius-control` and `--radius-panel` on the shared controls.
- **Mark.** The navbar 26, shown from `data-mark`.
- **Finish.** How solid the frame is: `solid`, `glass`, `cartoon`, `realistic`, `minimal`, or `extravagant`. Pick the one that fits the idea. `26 basic` stays `solid`. Glass keeps a readable plate over the ground, and reduced motion turns its blur off. Cartoon is a thick outline and a hard shadow, with no bounce. Realistic is depth only. A finish never outlines the heading, never covers an option, and never loops.
- **Motif.** An optional static icon on the ground: `none`, `crest`, `scatter`, or `bleed`. Use `none` when the ground pattern is already the picture, including `26 basic`. Company marks come from Simple Icons. Other motifs come from Lucide. The icon stays behind the question.

Question flow, scoring, and copy stay put. Do not add a looping animation on a control or a question. Reduced motion already removes the corner transition.

## Deep layer

A skin family also has a deep layer in `apps/web/src/theme/deep-skins.ts`, drawn by `theme-deep.css`. It goes beyond the surface, so two themes in different families feel like different products, not recolours. Every family except 26 basic's `plain` needs an entry; `deep-skins.test.ts` fails otherwise.

- **Type.** `grotesk`, `serif`, `mono`, `condensed`, `rounded`, `slab` or `italic`: sets `--font-display` and `--font-sans` and the heading case. Use system font stacks; do not load web fonts from the network.
- **Scene.** An illustrated background in the ground (spotlights, stars, falling code, an equaliser, a sunburst, confetti, doodles, lasers, hills, a synthwave grid, palms, a notebook, speed lines, shards, cubes, a road, receipts, a pub, a pitch, a globe). Built from the 24 `.deep-scene i` pieces, which carry `--x`, `--y`, `--s`, `--d` and `--r`. A scene may move slowly; keep anything behind a title faint, and keep bright shapes off the left third where titles sit.
- **Texture.** A faint full-screen layer over the page, like a shader: `grain`, `scanlines`, `crt`, `halftone`, `vignette` or `holo`. It ignores the pointer. Keep it light: the edges of the page carry text, so a vignette darkens corners only.
- **Control and panel.** The shape, edge and lighting of buttons (`neon`, `bevel`, `hard-shadow`, `slant`, `bracket`, `scoreboard`, `stamp`, `pill-glass`) and cards (`glass`, `double`, `taped`, `terminal`, `tilted`, `receipt`, `notebook`, `jagged`, `scoreboard`, `polaroid`).
- **Heading.** How question and page titles are dressed: `shadow-stack`, `glow`, `gradient`, `highlighter`, `prompt`, `ransom`, `stamp`, `marquee` or `underline`. The text must stay as readable as plain.
- **Motion.** The `--ease-party` curve and how a panel arrives, once: `snappy`, `springy`, `floaty`, `glitchy`, `cinematic` or `mechanical`.
- **Align.** Headings `left` or `center`.
- **Phone.** The same control and panel values dress the guest phone: the phone bar and dock, choice tiles and their letter marks, the picked state, the slider thumb and track, and text fields. A new control or panel value needs its phone rules too, and an option's text stays upright and on one layer.

Choose the combination for the idea, not the last family. A new value goes in both `deep-skins.ts` and `theme-deep.css`, built only from the theme's colour variables. Reduced motion stops every scene and texture animation, turns panel arrivals into a short fade, and turns off glass blur.

## Icons

Icon packs are installed in `@26/web`. Search the live set before adding an icon, and import one icon at a time. Do not trace a logo from a brand site or a fan page. If Simple Icons has no slug, say so and use a generic icon.

Render with the offline Iconify component so a missing icon does not call the network:

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@iconify/react/dist/offline";
import car from "@iconify-icons/lucide/car";

<Icon icon={car} />;
```

From the repo root, the pinned installs are:

```
npm install @iconify/react@6.0.2 -w @26/web
npm install @iconify-icons/lucide@2.0.13 -w @26/web
npm install @iconify-icons/simple-icons@2.0.4 -w @26/web
npm install @iconify-icons/game-icons@2.0.0 -w @26/web
npm install @iconify-icons/mdi@2.0.0 -w @26/web
```

The import path is `@iconify-icons/{prefix}/{icon-name}`.

| Category                                                                                                                                            | Pack                                                           | Look for                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 26 basic, Personal to 26, Quiz and chaos, Dark and atmospheric, Light and nostalgic, Personal to the night, Everyday, School, Work, Musicians, Cars | [Lucide](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/lucide/)             | circle, user, circle-help, moon, sun, star, coffee, graduation-cap, briefcase, music, car |
| Cars, Work, Musicians, Games, and any named company, bank, platform, or artist                                                                      | [Simple Icons](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/simple-icons/) | nissan, toyota, and the brand slug                                                        |
| Games, and a pictogram that is not a publisher logo                                                                                                 | [Game Icons](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/game-icons/)     | dice, swords, cards                                                                       |
| A shape Lucide does not have                                                                                                                        | [Material Design Icons](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/mdi/) | the closest generic glyph                                                                 |

Persona, Anime, and Crossovers use Lucide for the tab. Use Simple Icons only when that studio, series, or platform has a slug. Game Icons does not include franchise characters.

The favicon stays the 26 basic mark.

## Check

- `npx tsc -b apps/web`
- `npx vitest run src/theme` in `apps/web` (skins and deep skins)
- Preview with `?theme=its-id` and confirm the ground, corners, mark, and finish are visible while the question text stays readable. If the theme has a motif, the icon shows in the margin and a point on the heading still hits the heading.

### Render budgets, memoisation, layout, perceived performance, phone UX

Applies to `apps/web/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/**/*.css`.

# Web rendering and phone UX

Target: mid-range Android/iPhone on venue Wi-Fi. A question, lobby, or score beat must stay at **60 fps** when the phone is idle-to-tapping, and must not drop the tap-to-paint of the send control below one frame. The projector follows the same rule with larger type.

## State placement and re-renders

Put **high-frequency values in refs**, not in React state. Kart pose, clock remainder, pointer position, and Stockfish search flags update too often to re-render the tree.

```tsx
// ❌ BAD — every race tick rebuilds React
function Hud({ race }: { race: KartRaceView }) {
  const [now, setNow] = useState(0);
  useEffect(() => {
    const id = setInterval(() => setNow(Date.now()), 50);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  }, []);
  return <p>{now}</p>;
}

// ✅ GOOD — KartCanvas already keeps `live.current = race` and draws in rAF
useEffect(() => {
  live.current = race;
}, [race]);
```

Good pattern: `apps/web/src/kart/KartCanvas.tsx` (refs + rAF). Good pattern: `applySnapshotPatch` in `apps/web/src/live/room-socket.ts` keeps unchanged snapshot field identities so a clock patch does not redraw every player and option.

```tsx
// ❌ BAD — new object/function every snapshot, even when play is unchanged
<GuestPlay snapshot={snapshot} onSubmit={() => submit()} />;

// ✅ GOOD — stable handlers; split context so a kart frame does not refresh the dock
const onSubmit = useCallback(
  () => socket.submitAnswer(selectedId),
  [socket, selectedId],
);
```

Do not lift the whole `LobbySnapshot` through a provider that wraps chrome + question + trolls + media. Split by change rate: connection, play, self answer, trolls.

`memo` is for **lists of 80** (name cloud, standings, wall) and for round controls whose parent updates on patches. It is not a default wrapper for every file.

## Layout thrash

Do not read layout and write style in the same frame (`offsetWidth` then `style.left`, `getBoundingClientRect` in render, `scrollHeight` loops). Animate with Motion / CSS transforms, not top/left. Reserve space for images, avatars, and the phone dock so options do not jump (CLS).

```css
/* ❌ BAD */
.option img {
  height: auto;
}

/* ✅ GOOD — question option images have a known box before decode */
.option img {
  aspect-ratio: 1;
  width: 100%;
  height: auto;
}
```

Good pattern: `preloadImages` / `usePreloadQuestion` in `apps/web/src/play/preload.ts` fetch the **current** question’s pictures during intro, not the rest of the pack.

## Perceived performance

- Press, select, and send must change paint in the same gesture. Pending vs accepted stays distinct; never label a local tap “locked in”.
- Route and round `Suspense` fallbacks are real chrome (status text in the question frame), not a blank screen.
- Reconnect copy lives in `ReconnectBanner`: keep retrying, tell the guest after 1.5s, offer a manual retry later. Do not block the last known question behind a full-screen spinner.
- Honour `prefers-reduced-motion`. Loops, parallax, and layout travel belong off the answering controls.

## Touch and readability

- Primary hit targets stay large (existing dock and option tiles). `touch-action: manipulation` on tap controls so iOS does not wait for a double-tap zoom.
- Check 320 / 390 / 430px widths, safe areas, and a short landscape viewport. Do not shrink essential text to avoid scrolling; scroll vertically rather than clip.
- Do not `preventDefault` on `touchmove` unless you are the kart stick, and then only on that element.
- Projector type stays readable across a room. Secrets, host diagnostics, and answer keys never render on `/screen`.

## Lists of eighty

Keys are stable player ids, never array index. Do not run `layout` / `popLayout` animations on every tick for the full lobby. Name-cloud springs on **join/leave** are fine; animating size of all 80 bubbles every like-patch is not.

```tsx
// ❌ BAD — new array + index keys on every snapshot
names.map((name, i) => <li key={i}>{name.nickname}</li>)

// ✅ GOOD — NameCloud keys `name.playerId` and uses AnimatePresence for enter/exit
<CloudItem key={name.playerId} layout={!reduced ? "position" : false} />
```

## Effects, listeners, leaks

Every `addEventListener`, socket, `setTimeout`, rAF, `Worker`, `AudioContext`, wake lock, and `getUserMedia` stream is cleared in the same effect’s teardown. Do not subscribe in render. `openRoomSocket` already drops heartbeats and window listeners on close — call `close()` on unmount.

```tsx
// ❌ BAD
useEffect(() => {
  const engine = new StockfishEngine();
  void engine.initialize();
}, []);

// ✅ GOOD — chess-game must terminate the engine when the round or page goes away
useEffect(() => {
  const engine = new StockfishEngine({ onBestMove });
  void engine.initialize();
  return () => engine.terminate();
}, []);
```

### WebSocket messages, patches, reconnect, and 80-player fan-out

Applies to `apps/web/src/live/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/src/live/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/src/kart/useKartSocket.ts` and `apps/web/src/device/**/*.ts` and `apps/api/src/room/**/*.ts` and `packages/shared/src/**/*.ts`.

# Realtime messages (~80 phones)

There is **one** socket client: `openRoomSocket` in `apps/web/src/live/room-socket.ts`. There is **one** room object: `PartyRoom`. Do not add a second WebSocket, EventSource, or polling loop for live play.

Clients send **intents**. The room sends **snapshots, patches, kart frames, and acks**. Phones never invent phase, score, or clock.

## Size and shape

- Guest command bodies stay inside `maxPayloadBytes` (4 KiB) in `apps/api/src/room/limits.ts`. Do not attach photos, WAVs, or GLBs to a socket message; those go through the media upload path.
- Public snapshots are a **projection**. Guest and stage payloads must not include host-only fields, answer keys, or other players’ chess boards. Chess already splits guest / stage / control schemas — keep that split.
- Prefer a **patch** of changed top-level snapshot fields. `PartyRoom` already sends `kind: "patch"` when the patch is smaller than ~80% of a full snapshot. Do not add a new ad-hoc “delta” format beside it.
- A kart tick is `kind: "kart"`, merged with `mergeKartFrame`. It must not carry the lobby, media list, or question text. If the phone has no matching race snapshot, request a full snapshot — do not guess.

```ts
// ❌ BAD — 80 phones × full lobby on every race tick
send(ws, { kind: "snapshot", snapshot: buildSnapshot("guest", playerId) });

// ✅ GOOD — PartyRoom.broadcastKart + mergeKartFrame on the client
send(ws, { kind: "kart", ...frame });
```

## Frequency and batching

| Path                  | Budget                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Guest answers / votes | Token bucket `commandRateLimit` (burst 30, 3/s)                                                                             |
| Live drafts           | Debounce 200ms on the phone (`submitDraft`); `draftRateLimit` on the room                                                   |
| Kart inputs           | Client drops when `bufferedAmount >= 8192`; room `KartInputBuffer` keeps ≤4 per driver, ≥80ms apart, flush on the race tick |
| Clock probes          | Five on open, then with the 20s heartbeat (`timeRateLimit`)                                                                 |
| Device telemetry      | Phase change, resize (debounced), once a minute (`telemetryRateLimit`)                                                      |
| Broadcast coalescing  | `broadcastWindowMs = 30` so clustered writes share one fan-out                                                              |

```ts
// ❌ BAD — emit a draft on every keystroke
socket.send(JSON.stringify({ kind: "command", name: "draft", text }));

// ✅ GOOD — existing submitDraft leading-edge 200ms timer
```

Do not `requestSnapshot` in a loop, on every focus, or from a `setInterval`. The socket already asks once after a failed patch or a stale kart frame.

## Fan-out

Build **shared snapshot parts once per audience**, then specialise per guest (self answer, self chess, self troll). `snapshotParts` + `buildSnapshot` already do this. Do not run eighty identical SQL queries in a `for (const ws of sockets)` loop.

Eighty reconnects after a Wi-Fi blip must **jitter**. `reconnectDelay` uses full jitter capped at 8s. Do not reconnect on a fixed 100ms timer.

```ts
// ❌ BAD
setTimeout(connect, 100);

// ✅ GOOD
setTimeout(connect, reconnectDelay(attempt));
```

## Acks and optimism

Persist, then ack (`requestId`). Retries reuse the same idempotency key. The phone may show “sending”; it may not show “accepted” until `onAck`. Kart steering is the exception: local prediction in the canvas, room still owns the race.

## Diagnostics

`createRealtimeMeter` counts messages in memory for the host health view. Do not write those counters to SQLite on every send. Do not log full snapshots.

### Durable Object hot path, storage, alarms, and live-guest cost

Applies to `apps/api/**/*.ts` and `apps/api/src/questions/kart/**/*.ts` and `apps/api/src/questions/chess/**/*.ts` and `apps/api/src/room/kart/**/*.ts` and `packages/shared/**/*.ts`.

# Durable Object server hot path

One Worker, one SQLite-backed Durable Object per room (`PartyRoom`), one durable scheduler for alarms. Neon, Resend, and image/audio work stay **outside** the live guest-action path.

`packages/shared` logic takes `now: number`. Never call `Date.now()` inside reducers, scoring, or rate limits. The DO may read the clock at the edge and pass it in.

## Transactions and storage

SQLite on a DO is durable and not free. Each `storage.transactionSync` / SQL batch is work that **blocks the object** for every guest.

- Persist an accepted action **before** the success ack. Group the writes for one intent into **one** transaction (receipt, answer row, `state_version`, next alarm).
- Do not start a nested transaction per player in a fan-out.
- Memory is a cache (`KartIngressCache`, `KartInputBuffer`, rate buckets, last views). After a restart, rebuild from SQL; do not require the cache for correctness.
- Rate buckets live in memory (`maxRateBuckets = 400` for 80 phones × several names). Do not persist token buckets.

```ts
// ❌ BAD — SQL per socket while broadcasting
for (const ws of sockets) {
  const nickname = sql.exec("SELECT nickname FROM player WHERE player_id = ?", id);
  send(ws, nickname);
}

// ✅ GOOD — snapshotParts loads players once; buildSnapshot reuses parts
const parts = this.snapshotParts("guest", statistics);
```

`KartIngressCache` exists so unacked kart controls do not re-parse the roster. Do not delete it to “simplify”. Do not use it as authority for scoring.

## Alarms and ticks

`alarm()` runs due jobs in one `commitAndArm` transaction. A **kart race tick** (five times a second) must stay `raceTickOnly`: flush inputs, step the race, skip archive queries, and prefer `broadcastKart()` over a full snapshot.

```ts
// ❌ BAD — settle archive and rebuild guest snapshots 5×/s during a race
await settleArchive(...);
this.broadcast();

// ✅ GOOD — existing alarm() short-circuit
if (!raceTickOnly || !this.broadcastKart()) {
  this.broadcast(true);
}
```

Do not add a second `setTimeout` scheduler beside the durable alarm. Do not use `Date.now()` inside `reduceKart` / chess / troll reducers.

## CPU on the object

The DO is single-threaded for the room. A 20ms stall is 20ms of lag for 80 phones.

- Keep JSON.parse/stringify and Zod at the boundary, once per message.
- Do not run Stockfish, image codecs, or `jpeg-js` on the room object for a live tap.
- Chess move validation belongs in the mechanic; engine search belongs in the **phone worker**.
- Load tests: `npm run load:realtime -w @26/api`. A new broadcast or per-input SQL needs a thought for 80 senders.

## Effects after reduce

Shared helpers return `{ state, effects }`. The DO executes effects (broadcast, alarm, persist). Do not hide a broadcast inside a domain function that also writes SQL in a surprising second pass.

## Config

Read bindings from the request env. `no-restricted-syntax` already forbids `process.env` in `apps/api/src` and `packages/shared/src`. Local fakes must refuse to succeed when `APP_ENV` is `staging` or `production`.

### requestAnimationFrame, kart/chess/troll loops, workers and WASM

Applies to `apps/web/src/kart/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/src/kart/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/src/chess/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/src/chess/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/src/troll/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/src/troll/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/src/play/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/src/play/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/public/chess-engine/**` and `apps/web/public/kart-engine/**` and `packages/shared/src/kart/**/*.ts` and `packages/shared/src/chess/**/*.ts`.

# Game loops, workers, and WASM

React renders **beats** (intro, collect, reveal). Canvas, Stockfish, and particle systems render **frames**. Do not mix them.

## requestAnimationFrame

One rAF (or one Three.js `setAnimationLoop`) per visible canvas. Pause it when the tab is hidden, the round is paused, or the component unmounts. Never `setState` inside the frame callback.

```ts
// ❌ BAD
function tick() {
  setPose(readPose());
  requestAnimationFrame(tick);
}

// ✅ GOOD — KartCanvas: mutate Three objects from `live.current`, then render
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => {
  const race = live.current;
  // ...update meshes from race / prediction refs
  renderer.render(scene, camera);
});
```

`useKartControls` may poll gamepads in rAF; it must cancel the frame on disable. Troll overlays that use rAF (`screen-trolls`) must stop on effect cleanup and on reduced motion.

Clamp delta time so a backgrounded tab does not step 5s of physics on wake. The **room** still owns race time; the phone only interpolates public poses plus local self-prediction.

## Kart (Three.js)

- Import `three` only from `apps/web/src/kart/**`. Guest and stage entry must `lazy()` the canvas (`GuestPlay`, `KartDriverView`, `KartStageView`, `stage-play`).
- `warmKart()` during the kart **intro**, not at `/play` join (`usePreloadQuestion`).
- Bound work to **self + nearby** racers (`graphicsProfiles.nearbyLimit`). Do not draw 80 full vehicle rigs at phone resolution.
- Respect `safeGraphicsProfile` / frame probe: drop pixel ratio, sparks, and trails when the canvas is strained. Decoration never changes race state.
- On unmount: dispose geometries, materials, textures, renderer, and the animation loop (`KartCanvas` already disposes look, circuit, renderer).
- `powerPreference: "low-power"` on phones. No antialias on mobile.

## Chess (Stockfish WASM)

- Engine code stays in `apps/web/src/chess/stockfish-worker.ts` and `/chess-engine/`. Do not import the `stockfish` npm package from guest-play, stage, or admin chrome.
- Run UCI on a **Worker**. Never on the window thread.
- One init worker per mounted game. `terminate()` it on unmount, on round exit, and before creating a replacement. Isolate in-flight searches so a stale `bestmove` cannot apply; still **tear down** workers so a long game does not accumulate them.
- Warm the engine on chess intro / first board paint, with a visible “Loading chess engine…” fallback. Do not fetch the WASM on `/join`.
- The room validates moves and scores captures. The phone worker is a bot, not authority.

```ts
// ❌ BAD — leave workers alive when the guest leaves the round
await engine.initialize();

// ✅ GOOD
useEffect(() => {
  void engine.initialize();
  return () => engine.terminate();
}, [engine]);
```

## Trolls and VFX

Stage VFX and phone troll overlays must budget particles (`vfx-budget`, `kartVfxBudgets`). A troll that runs on 80 phones cannot allocate unbounded canvases or decode a unique video per guest. Prefer CSS/Motion on the phone; keep WebGL on the projector unless the troll is explicitly a phone effect.

Reduced motion: no loops, no screen shake that hides the question, no colour-only meaning.

### Bundle size, code-splitting, assets, caching, and startup

Applies to `apps/web/src/routes.tsx` and `apps/web/src/main.tsx` and `apps/web/src/play/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/src/play/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/src/guest/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/src/guest/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/src/stage/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/src/stage/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/vite.config.ts` and `apps/web/index.html` and `apps/web/public/**/*` and `packages/shared/src/**/*.ts`.

# Bundle, assets, and startup

Phones join on flaky venue Wi-Fi. The **first** JavaScript they need is: theme, join/play chrome, socket client, and the current ordinary question. Kart, chess, admin, Three, and Stockfish stay out of that graph.

## Code splitting

`apps/web/src/routes.tsx` already `lazy()`s `/play`, `/screen`, `/admin`, `/kart`, `/chess`. Keep it that way. A new round that pulls a heavy engine uses `React.lazy` **inside** the play renderer as well, like `GuestKart` / `GuestChess` in `guest-play.tsx`.

```tsx
// ❌ BAD — Three.js in the guest question module
import { KartCanvas } from "../kart/KartCanvas";

// ✅ GOOD
const GuestKart = lazy(() =>
  import("../kart/GuestKart").then((kart) => ({ default: kart.GuestKart })),
);
```

Do not import `apps/web/src/admin/**` from guest or stage. Do not import `apps/web/src/kart/**` or `apps/web/src/chess/**` from `main.tsx`, `routes.tsx` (except the dedicated `/kart` and `/chess` route factories), or the always-on theme install.

If you add a library, pin it, keep the lockfile, and check `npm run budget:web`. A new always-on import that blows the **entry JS gzip** budget is a failed change, not a warning to ignore.

Shared Zod schemas used on the phone must stay small. Do not re-export Node, Worker, or pack-private answer keys through `packages/shared/src/index.ts`.

## Images, audio, fonts

- Option images: current question only (`questionImages` / `preloadImages`). `decoding="async"`, width/height or aspect-ratio to avoid CLS.
- Do not ship new webfont files for a theme. Themes use system stacks in the deep skin. Existing `@fontsource` on the party chrome is enough; do not add a third family to the critical path without a budget pass.
- Audio is optional and behind a user gesture. Do not autoplay on join. Decode / fetch the sting when the round that needs it is announced.
- Photos go through the media pipeline and R2, not as base64 on the socket.
- Iconify: import **one** icon module at a time from `@iconify-icons/*` and render `@iconify/react/dist/offline`. Do not load the Iconify CDN.

## Caching and public engines

`/chess-engine/` and `/kart-engine/` are static. They must remain cache-friendly (stable filenames hashed or versioned by the build that copies them). Fetch them only when that round is active or warming.

Do not commit generated `apps/web/public/kart-engine/` output; the web `prebuild` rebuilds it.

## Startup / TTI

- `/play` must paint join or the current beat without waiting for kart WASM/GLB or Stockfish.
- Avoid giant JSON in the first module. Question packs stay on the server; the phone receives the projected question in the snapshot.
- Service workers: do not add one unless the owner asked. A stale SW on 80 phones is worse than a cold load.
- Measure with `npm run perf:audit` against a preview when you change the entry graph. Do not add Playwright specs for it.

## Budget gate

`scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs` (via `npm run build` / `npm run budget:web`) reads `apps/web/dist/client` and fails CI when gzip sizes exceed `scripts/web-bundle-budget.json`. If a genuine feature needs more bytes, **raise the budget in the same PR** and say why in the PR body. Do not delete the check.

## Paths to leave closed

Do not open, quote, or modify these paths.

- `node_modules/`
- `dist/`
- `.wrangler/`
- `**/.mf/`
- `.vite/`
- `.data/`
- `coverage/`
- `playwright-report/`
- `test-results/`
- `blob-report/`
- `*.tsbuildinfo`
- `.dev.vars`
- `.dev.vars.*`
- `.dev.vars.staging`
- `.dev.vars.production`
- `.env`
- `.env.*`
- `.env.local`
- `.env.staging`
- `.env.production`
- `**/*.pem`
- `**/*.key`
- `**/credentials.json`
- `**/secrets.json`

These example files may be read:

- `.dev.vars.example`
- `.env.example`
